passages.original: ἄνευ Σοφοκλέους ὅ τι ποιεῖ κωδωνίσω.
passages.english: [to see] what he can do without Sophocles, I'll ring him [like a coin, to test him].
passages.notes: κωδωνίσω: literally 'test by ringing', as one tests a coin or vessel for soundness, i.e. sound him out. The line in Frogs (Heracles on Iophon, ca. 79) reads ἄνευ Σοφοκλέους ὅ τι ποιεῖ κωδωνίσαι, with an infinitive ('to sound out'); this text has the first-person future κωδωνίσω. The line is a fragment without context.

passages.original: δὶς ταὐτὸν ἡμῖν εἶπεν ὁ σοφὸς Αἰσχύλος.
passages.english: The clever Aeschylus has told us the same thing twice.
